deepdive.sec: Digital Local Search & SME Advertising Platform

bull_bear.body: No formal policy yet; Board and parent (Reliance) reviewing cash return strategy; likely dividend (tax-efficient) to be announced by Q2FY26; prior proposal was 100% PAT payout; excess cash: INR5,279cr as of March 2025
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Competition from Google Maps/IndiaMART on search accuracy; potential user frustration with outdated listings; B2B sales complexity requiring specialized training; delayed dividend announcement affecting investor sentiment; AI adoption may require significant tech investment
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, pragmatic, and focused on sustainable growth; management emphasizes efficiency over brute-force expansion, acknowledges past underperformance in top-line growth, and is now pivoting to monetization levers (pricing, ads, new product) with clear intent to return cash
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Dynamic pricing in non-premium listings (50% of revenue) is a hidden margin lever — pricing now varies by keyword (e.g., grocery vs real estate), not just geography, enabling 7-8% blended price increase without volume loss; AI is already reducing manual data entry and improving sales conversion via intent scoring
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Cash & Investments (period end) rise in each of the nine quarters shown, from Rs 47,555 million in 1Q FY25 to Rs 60,221 million in 1Q FY27 (+10.9% YoY, +2.9% QoQ).
- Treasury is a material earnings driver: "Other Income primarily constitutes mark-to-market (MTM) gains on treasury portfolio, which can have high quarterly fluctuations depending on movement of bond yields during that quarter."
- Prepaid/unearned revenue funds working capital: Unearned Revenue (period end) of Rs 5,401 million versus Rs 5,346 million a year earlier and Rs 5,554 million in 4Q FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- One of the country's largest databases of local enterprises, built over more than three decades
- Verified ratings, reviews and multimedia content — total ratings and reviews of 157.1 million and active business listings of 54.7 million
- Pan-India merchant network with field and tele-sales teams extending well into Tier II and Tier III markets
- Proprietary technology, with AI-led discovery ('Ask Anything', multilingual and voice search, semantic and vector models) and an MCP framework allowing external AI engines to access Justdial data securely
- Subscription-led, debt-free financial model funded by advance collections under a prepaid subscription model, supporting negative working capital and strong revenue visibility
- Long-standing local database, ongoing product enhancement and a diversified category mix that the Company describes as difficult to replicate
- Treasury and investment corpus providing a liquidity cushion and capacity to reinvest in technology, sales capability and product development
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data privacy and protection — The Company holds user and business data at scale; it names controlled access, strict safeguards, an ISMS framework and security systems as the controls that reduce the risk of breaches.
- Competition — Flagged as a principal risk in the MD&A risk table; the stated defence is a long-standing local database, ongoing product enhancement and a diversified category mix creating scale and depth the Company describes as difficult to replicate.
- Operational — keeping the platform aligned to changing user needs — Mitigated by continuous tracking of user behaviour and product development across JD Mart, JD Omni and JD Pay.
- Technological — reliability, security and scalability amid rapid technological change — Mitigated by dedicated teams and ongoing system upgrades; the platform runs on cloud and on-premise infrastructure and is shifting to AI-led discovery.
- Geographical concentration on top metro clusters — The Company names sales expansion across Tier II and Tier III cities as the means of broadening reach and reducing dependence on top metro clusters.
- Economic cycles affecting merchant affordability and retention — Listed as a principal risk; the mitigation text is cut off mid-word in this bundle ('Flexible subscription structur'), but the readable part points to flexible subscription structures, a diversified customer base and long-standing relationships.
- Single-segment concentration — The MD&A states 'We operate in a single reporting segment named Search and Search-related Services' — there is no second segment to offset a downturn in local search monetisation. The AR does not label this as a risk.
- Enterprise-wide risk exposures overseen by the Risk Management Committee — The Board's Report enumerates strategic, financial, market, security, operational, personnel, IT, legal, regulatory and reputational risks as the categories the Committee oversees, without sizing any of them.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Top 11 cities: 56.5% of Q4 revenue (down from 58% YoY); B2B revenue: 26.5% of total (stable); B2B traffic: 20% of total traffic (up from 15%); non-premium listings: 50% of revenue; mobile traffic: 87% of total, growing 15% YoY

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims "First Mover Advantage in Indian Local Search Market" with "Strong Brand Recognition with 192.9 million unique quarterly visitors^ in Q1 FY27 (182.4 million in Q4 FY26)"; the footnote states unique visitors are aggregated across Voice, Desktop/PC and Mobile and "may not necessarily be mutually exclusive".
- Moat is framed as data depth: "Database of 56.1 million listings", "High user engagement, 160.5 million ratings & reviews" and Total Images in Listings of 262.9 million (period end, 1Q FY27).
- Three-platform reach with Q1 FY27 traffic share of Mobile 86.5%, Desktop/PC 10.6% and Voice 2.9% (single pan-India hotline 88888-88888, 24x7, multi-lingual).
- Other stated strengths: "Attractive Value Proposition For Local SMEs", "Advanced and Scalable Technology Platform", "Efficient & Profitable Business Model" and "Strong Financial Profile, Prepaid Model".
- Shareholding as on Jun 30, 2026: Promoter and Promoter Group 74.14%, of which "Stake held by Promoter - Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL) = 63.83%"; Domestic Investors 4.01%, Individuals 10.23%, Foreign Investors 11.62% (deck's percentage-to-label placement for the three non-promoter buckets is not fully unambiguous in the extract).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership transition] "Mr. Dinkar Ayilavarapu has been appointed as Chief Executive Officer (designate) and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company w.e.f. July 10, 2026. He shall take over as Chief Executive Officer and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company effective August 1, 2026. Mr. V.S.S. Mani completes his term as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Company on July 31, 2026."
- [CFO change] "Mr. Dinesh Taluja has resigned as Non-Executive Director of the Company with effect from close of business hours on July 10, 2026 and he is appointed as Chief Financial Officer and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company w.e.f. July 11, 2026."
- [Regulation] New labour code on Social Security, 2020, effective November 21, 2025, amended the definition of "wages" for gratuity and expanded coverage to fixed-term employees; "the Company has recognized a one-time, past service cost of Rs 210.8 million on account of aforesaid revision as Exceptional item" for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 and year ended March 31, 2026.
- [Deck contradiction - listings] The company-overview page states a "Database of 56.1 million listings" (and the summary table shows Total Listings of 56.1 million at 1Q FY27 end), while the Key Strengths page on the same deck states a "Comprehensive database of 54.7 million listings" (the 4Q FY26 figure).
- [Deck contradiction - salesforce] The company-overview page states "5,796 employees in tele-sales, 5,169 feet-on-street salesforce", while the business-model page splits the same period as "5,796 employees in tele-sales, 1,539 feet-on-street (marketing), and 3,630 feet-on-street (Cold Calling & Others) as on Q1 FY27".
- [Board composition] Non-executive directors are drawn from the Reliance group (V. Subramaniam, MD of Reliance Retail Ventures Limited; Ashwin Khasgiwala; Geeta Fulwadaya; Anshuman Thakur of Jio Platforms), alongside four independent directors chaired by Krishnan Sudarshan.
- [Listing venues] The covering letter is addressed to BSE (Scrip Code 535648), NSE and the Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India (Trading Symbol JUSTDIAL on both NSE and MSE).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Justdial connects users searching for trusted local products and services with the businesses that provide them, across categories, geographies and access points. Users reach the platform through Android and iOS apps, mobile site, desktop, conversational interfaces including WhatsApp, and the 88888 88888 voice hotline, supported by a verified ratings-and-reviews framework and structured enquiry tools such as Request for Quotes. On the merchant side an integrated suite spans listing, lead management, websites, payments, analytics and B2B commerce, monetised through a prepaid, subscription-led model; the Company reports a single segment named Search and Search-related Services.

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin ~55%; EBITDA margin at 29.4% (FY25) and 29.8% (Q4); operating leverage allows 1-2% A&P increase without margin erosion; cost control achieved via elimination of cold-calling sales team (2.5-3x productivity gain with qualified leads)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: target mid-teens (12-15%) in FY26; margin: sustain 28-30%; order inflow: no explicit target; capex/commissioning: minimal, focused on tech/AI, no major CAPEX planned
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Launch of Just Dial Online Shopping platform (beta next quarter) to capture B2C/B2B online sellers; monetization via commission/referral after traction; AI-enhanced product cataloging and video generation for listings; dynamic pricing in non-premium categories (50% of revenue) to boost ARPU
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Make discovery simpler, quicker and more context-aware by interpreting intent rather than matching keywords — AI-led capabilities across search, recommendations and content including 'Ask Anything', multilingual discovery, voice interactions, predictive suggestions and AI-generated review summaries, with semantic and vector-based models for conversational queries
- Reduce merchant turnaround time through automated onboarding, instant KYC, AI-assisted catalogue creation and intelligent lead management
- Consolidate the most-used merchant capabilities into single integrated launches rather than scattered releases — the JD Sixer Pack brought parallel calling, leads dashboard, CRM tools, review management, business dashboard and competition trends into one product, supported by an educational video series and in-product walkthroughs
- Widen adoption of Universal Business Listing so merchants manage listings and reputation across Justdial, Google, Instagram, WhatsApp Business and Facebook from one dashboard
- Deepen MSME participation through the integrated suite of JD Business, JD Omni, JD Pay, JD Analytics and JD Mart, letting merchants enter digital commerce without complex technology adoption
- Keep the physical footprint as a differentiator — combine nationwide digital reach with local field presence and an extensive service network, particularly in Tier II and Tier III cities where vernacular adoption is widening digital participation
- Strengthen marketplace trust — authenticated ratings and reviews, field verification with shopfront and signage imagery, fraud-monitoring systems, cross-platform validation and the JD Verified and JD Trust badges awarded only after KYC verification
- Support merchants across the Build, Grow and Sustain stages, including 24x7 assistance across calls, a self-serve portal and WhatsApp
- Sustain brand recall through content and outreach programmes and the return of the 88888 88888 radio campaign
- The Board's Report states that no amount was transferred to the Reserves of the Company during the year under review. The Company maintains a Dividend Distribution Policy, published on its website; the policy's contents are not reproduced in this bundle and no payout ratio, buyback, debt-reduction or reinvestment philosophy is stated here. Related-party contracts are stated to be in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis, with none material enough to require Form AOC-2 reporting. The Company states it had no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company as at March 31, 2026, and accordingly prepared no consolidated financial statements.
- CSR effort is directed primarily towards education, where the Company states it has invested in improving access to quality education for the underprivileged; the CSR Policy is unchanged from the prior year. No ESG target, baseline or timeline is stated — the BRSR itself is hosted on the Company's website and is not present in this bundle.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Justdial is asset-light: the Annual Report describes footprint and platform build-out rather than plants or capacity. Deployed resources are listed as the JD App, JD Mart, JD Omni, JD Pay, JD Ratings, JD Analytics and JD Business platforms, cloud-based technology platforms and on-premise servers, the pan-India operator-assisted helpline 88888 88888, and 11 branch offices across India's key cities. Reach spans over 250 cities and 11,000-plus pin codes, supported by a workforce of 13,070 employees as on March 31, 2026 — 5,350 in the feet-on-street salesforce, 5,122 in tele-sales and 2,598 in support, voice, content, product and technology. The stated growth opportunity is 'strategic expansion into under-penetrated Tier II and Tier III segments, where 90%+ MSMEs accept digital payments, but only 13% use digital marketing'. On technology absorption, the Board's Report says the Company undertook focused initiatives to enhance the AI readiness of its technology workforce and infrastructure through targeted upskilling, modernisation of technology platforms and adoption of AI-enabled development tools, and continues to integrate AI across product development and engineering; it has developed most of its software and apps in-house. The report explicitly states there was no capital investment on energy conservation equipment during the year, no technology imported during the last three years, and no expenditure incurred on Research and Development during the year under review. It also states the Company had no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company as at March 31, 2026, so no expansion through those routes is described. Funds raised in FY 2021-22 through the preferential allotment to Reliance Retail Ventures Limited remain, pending utilisation, temporarily deployed in mutual funds and fixed deposits, with no deviation in the use of proceeds. No named capex project, commissioning date or ramp timeline is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The structural shift towards digital ecosystems is the material read-through: deeper reliance on platform-based discovery and SME digitisation strengthens the Company's relevance, while a predominantly domestic, consumption-led model limits direct exposure to global volatility
- Broad-based Indian expansion widens Justdial's addressable market — a more diverse enterprise base deepens listings across B2B and consumer categories, while rising consumption and formalisation increase both search activity and merchants' willingness to invest in digital visibility
- Digital-economy enablers (internet subscribers past one billion, 5G, BharatNet, data-centre capacity, Global Capability Centres) translate into higher search intensity, broader business participation and deeper penetration of non-metro markets
- Telecom and internet shifts — broadband subscribers at 1,065.9 million as of March 2026, 5G across nearly all districts, UPI at 21.7 billion transactions in January 2026, and AI embedded in consumer and enterprise applications — enlarge the addressable user base, raise engagement intensity and tighten the link between discovery and transaction, supporting deeper market penetration and stronger monetisation
- Convergence of MSME formalisation, digital infrastructure and policy-led credit is structurally favourable: it enlarges the base of potential advertisers and service providers and lifts demand for digital discovery, lead generation and performance-driven marketing
- Rural tele-density well below urban levels is described as signalling substantial headroom for incremental adoption
- India's local discovery landscape is entering a new stage shaped by conversational interfaces, AI-assisted interactions and wider digital participation across emerging markets
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Just Dial delivered strong margin expansion (29.4% EBITDA margin) and cash flow growth despite modest top-line growth, but now has clear levers to accelerate revenue via dynamic pricing, higher ad spend, and a new online shopping platform launching next quarter — all while maintaining profitability and preparing for a long-awaited cash return policy.

open.item: Deepen user engagement and expand reach — the first of three stated drivers under 'What drives us forward'.
Accelerate merchant monetisation — the second of three stated drivers under 'What drives us forward'.
Invest in AI and platform intelligence — the third of three stated drivers under 'What drives us forward'.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's leading local search platform, operating a two-sided marketplace at the intersection of consumer intent and India's MSME economy.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Justdial connects users searching for trusted local products and services with the businesses that provide them, across categories, geographies and access points. Users reach the platform through Android and iOS apps, mobile site, desktop, conversational interfaces including WhatsApp, and the 88888 88888 voice hotline, supported by a verified ratings-and-reviews framework and structured enquiry tools such as Request for Quotes. On the merchant side an integrated suite spans listing, lead management, websites, payments, analytics and B2B commerce, monetised through a prepaid, subscription-led model; the Company reports a single segment named Search and Search-related Services.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Top 11 cities: 56.5% of Q4 revenue (down from 58% YoY); B2B revenue: 26.5% of total (stable); B2B traffic: 20% of total traffic (up from 15%); non-premium listings: 50% of revenue; mobile traffic: 87% of total, growing 15% YoY

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Search and Search-related Services:** JD App and discovery interfaces (Android, iOS, mobile site, desktop), 88888 88888 voice hotline, 'Ask Anything' AI-led search, Request for Quotes (RFQ), JD Ratings & Reviews, JD Verified and JD Trust badges, JD Business, JD Omni, JD Pay, JD Analytics, JD Mart, Universal Business Listing (UBL), JD Sixer Pack, Travel, Bills & Recharge

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India — pan-India local search, no international operations described
- Reach spanning over 250 cities and 11,000-plus pin codes
- Tier II and Tier III markets, served by field and tele-sales teams
- MSMEs and SMEs seeking digital visibility and leads
- B2B buyers, manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and retailers via JD Mart
- Consumers searching for local products and services

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: target mid-teens (12-15%) in FY26; margin: sustain 28-30%; order inflow: no explicit target; capex/commissioning: minimal, focused on tech/AI, no major CAPEX planned

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Launch of Just Dial Online Shopping platform (beta next quarter) to capture B2C/B2B online sellers; monetization via commission/referral after traction; AI-enhanced product cataloging and video generation for listings; dynamic pricing in non-premium categories (50% of revenue) to boost ARPU

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The structural shift towards digital ecosystems is the material read-through: deeper reliance on platform-based discovery and SME digitisation strengthens the Company's relevance, while a predominantly domestic, consumption-led model limits direct exposure to global volatility
- Broad-based Indian expansion widens Justdial's addressable market — a more diverse enterprise base deepens listings across B2B and consumer categories, while rising consumption and formalisation increase both search activity and merchants' willingness to invest in digital visibility
- Digital-economy enablers (internet subscribers past one billion, 5G, BharatNet, data-centre capacity, Global Capability Centres) translate into higher search intensity, broader business participation and deeper penetration of non-metro markets
- Telecom and internet shifts — broadband subscribers at 1,065.9 million as of March 2026, 5G across nearly all districts, UPI at 21.7 billion transactions in January 2026, and AI embedded in consumer and enterprise applications — enlarge the addressable user base, raise engagement intensity and tighten the link between discovery and transaction, supporting deeper market penetration and stronger monetisation
- Convergence of MSME formalisation, digital infrastructure and policy-led credit is structurally favourable: it enlarges the base of potential advertisers and service providers and lifts demand for digital discovery, lead generation and performance-driven marketing
- Rural tele-density well below urban levels is described as signalling substantial headroom for incremental adoption
- India's local discovery landscape is entering a new stage shaped by conversational interfaces, AI-assisted interactions and wider digital participation across emerging markets

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin ~55%; EBITDA margin at 29.4% (FY25) and 29.8% (Q4); operating leverage allows 1-2% A&P increase without margin erosion; cost control achieved via elimination of cold-calling sales team (2.5-3x productivity gain with qualified leads)

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: No formal policy yet; Board and parent (Reliance) reviewing cash return strategy; likely dividend (tax-efficient) to be announced by Q2FY26; prior proposal was 100% PAT payout; excess cash: INR5,279cr as of March 2025

capex_expansion.body: Justdial is asset-light: the Annual Report describes footprint and platform build-out rather than plants or capacity. Deployed resources are listed as the JD App, JD Mart, JD Omni, JD Pay, JD Ratings, JD Analytics and JD Business platforms, cloud-based technology platforms and on-premise servers, the pan-India operator-assisted helpline 88888 88888, and 11 branch offices across India's key cities. Reach spans over 250 cities and 11,000-plus pin codes, supported by a workforce of 13,070 employees as on March 31, 2026 — 5,350 in the feet-on-street salesforce, 5,122 in tele-sales and 2,598 in support, voice, content, product and technology. The stated growth opportunity is 'strategic expansion into under-penetrated Tier II and Tier III segments, where 90%+ MSMEs accept digital payments, but only 13% use digital marketing'. On technology absorption, the Board's Report says the Company undertook focused initiatives to enhance the AI readiness of its technology workforce and infrastructure through targeted upskilling, modernisation of technology platforms and adoption of AI-enabled development tools, and continues to integrate AI across product development and engineering; it has developed most of its software and apps in-house. The report explicitly states there was no capital investment on energy conservation equipment during the year, no technology imported during the last three years, and no expenditure incurred on Research and Development during the year under review. It also states the Company had no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company as at March 31, 2026, so no expansion through those routes is described. No named capex project, commissioning date or ramp timeline is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, pragmatic, and focused on sustainable growth; management emphasizes efficiency over brute-force expansion, acknowledges past underperformance in top-line growth, and is now pivoting to monetization levers (pricing, ads, new product) with clear intent to return cash

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the country's largest databases of local enterprises, built over more than three decades
- Verified ratings, reviews and multimedia content — total ratings and reviews of 157.1 million and active business listings of 54.7 million
- Pan-India merchant network with field and tele-sales teams extending well into Tier II and Tier III markets
- Proprietary technology, with AI-led discovery ('Ask Anything', multilingual and voice search, semantic and vector models) and an MCP framework allowing external AI engines to access Justdial data securely
- Subscription-led, debt-free financial model funded by advance collections under a prepaid subscription model, supporting negative working capital and strong revenue visibility
- Long-standing local database, ongoing product enhancement and a diversified category mix that the Company describes as difficult to replicate
- Treasury and investment corpus providing a liquidity cushion and capacity to reinvest in technology, sales capability and product development

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Competition from Google Maps/IndiaMART on search accuracy; potential user frustration with outdated listings; B2B sales complexity requiring specialized training; delayed dividend announcement affecting investor sentiment; AI adoption may require significant tech investment

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Dynamic pricing in non-premium listings (50% of revenue) is a hidden margin lever — pricing now varies by keyword (e.g., grocery vs real estate), not just geography, enabling 7-8% blended price increase without volume loss; AI is already reducing manual data entry and improving sales conversion via intent scoring

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Make discovery simpler, quicker and more context-aware by interpreting intent rather than matching keywords — AI-led capabilities across search, recommendations and content including 'Ask Anything', multilingual discovery, voice interactions, predictive suggestions and AI-generated review summaries, with semantic and vector-based models for conversational queries
- Reduce merchant turnaround time through automated onboarding, instant KYC, AI-assisted catalogue creation and intelligent lead management
- Consolidate the most-used merchant capabilities into single integrated launches rather than …

challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google Maps and IndiaMART offer more accurate local search results | IndiaMART | loser | Medium | Just Dial's new online shopping platform may cannibalize IndiaMART's SME seller base |
| Reliance's delayed capital allocation decision | Reliance Industries | beneficiary | High | Just Dial's cash return policy (likely dividend) will unlock value for Reliance as parent holding 70%+ stake |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership transition] "Mr. Dinkar Ayilavarapu has been appointed as Chief Executive Officer (designate) and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company w.e.f. July 10, 2026. He shall take over as Chief Executive Officer and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company effective August 1, 2026. Mr. V.S.S. Mani completes his term as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Company on July 31, 2026."
- [CFO change] "Mr. Dinesh Taluja has resigned as Non-Executive Director of the Company with effect from close of business hours on July 10, 2026 and he is appointed as Chief Financial Officer and Key Managerial Personnel of the Company w.e.f. July 11, 2026."
- [Regulation] New labour code on Social Security, 2020, effective November 21, 2025, amended the definition of "wages" for gratuity and expanded coverage to fixed-term employees; "the Company has recognized a one-time, past service cost of Rs 210.8 million on account of aforesaid revision as Exceptional item" for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 and year ended March 31, 2026.
- [Deck contradiction - listings] The company-overview page states a "Database of 56.1 million listings" (and the summary table shows Total Listings of 56.1 million at 1Q FY27 end), while the Key Strengths page on the same deck states a "Comprehensive database of 54.7 million listings" (the 4Q FY26 figure).
- [Deck contradiction - salesforce] The company-overview page states "5,796 employees in tele-sales, 5,169 feet-on-street salesforce", while the business-model page splits the same period as "5,796 employees in tele-sales, 1,539 feet-on-street (marketing), and 3,630 feet-on-street (Cold Calling & Others) as on Q1 FY27".
- [Board composition] Non-executive directors are drawn from the Reliance group (V. Subramaniam, MD of Reliance Retail Ventures Limited; Ashwin Khasgiwala; Geeta Fulwadaya; Anshuman Thakur of Jio Platforms), alongside four independent directors chaired by Krishnan Sudarshan.
- [Listing venues] The covering letter is addressed to BSE (Scrip Code 535648), NSE and the Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India (Trading Symbol JUSTDIAL on both NSE and MSE).

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

themes.title: Digital adtech & programmatic
themes.need: Digital adtech players ride performance/programmatic ad-spend, app-install and user-acquisition monetization with AI-creative optimization - a structural digital-shift thesis distinct from the cyclical traditional-media ad-recovery.
themes.driver: Programmatic/performance ad-spend, app-install monetization and AI-creative optimization.
